state.misconception_label: Assumes that an arrow on a number line starts at zero

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: ![Number line with -12 and -7 marked. Starting at -12, follow an arrow pointing to the right labelled +10. Then there is an arrow labelled b pointing to the left, which ends at -7 on the number line.]() What is the value of \( b \) ? I got \( -7 \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: You are assuming that the arrow on the number line starts at zero. Remember, when working with a number line, the starting point of the arrow does not necessarily indicate zero. Let's revisit the steps together to correctly determine the value of \( b \).

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so the arrow doesn't start at zero... so I need to figure out where it actually starts from? So like, the first arrow starts at -12 and goes right by +10, so that would take me to -2, and then the second arrow b goes left from there to -7? Is that how I'm supposed to work it out?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: You are on the right track. Remember, when moving on a number line, it's important to consider the direction and magnitude of each movement. Can you now apply this concept to correctly determine the value of \( b \)?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: So if I start at -12 and go right by +10, I get to -2, and then arrow b goes left from -2 to -7... so that means b must be -5? Like, I'm moving 5 places to the left, so is b = -5?
